title: Profile-aware pin resolver: prioritize pins by provenance, semver ranges, and performance profiles
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define and implement SDK + runtime semantics for resolving model pins when consumers specify tags, semver ranges, commit hashes, or performance-profile selectors. Ensure deterministic resolution, clear precedence rules, auditability, and safe fallbacks that respect published performance profiles and provenance metadata.
acceptance_criteria: SDK accepts pin types: tag, semver (exact and range), commit_hash (full or prefix), and profile_selector.
Runtime resolver deterministically returns a single model artifact reference (immutable digest) for any legal pin input and logs resolution path in audit logs.

Pinned-by-profile mode picks a model variant compatible with requested perf profile (latency/cost/throughput) and matches other constraints; if none available uses strict fallback chain documented below.
Semver range resolution follows defined compatibility policy (caret-style by default) and prefers highest matching patch, then minor, then major as configured by project policy.

Conflict cases (e.g., tag pointing to multiple artifacts, stale tags, ambiguous short commit hashes) surface as a 409 with resolution hints in API response and a stable CLI flag to force exact digest.
Performance profile metadata is published alongside model artifacts and surfaced through the Model Catalog API; SDK provides helper to evaluate match quality.
Security: resolver verifies signed provenance when 'require_signed' flag is set and rejects unsigned artifacts when policy demands it.
decisions: Precedence order: exact digest -> commit_hash (full match) -> tag (annotated with timestamp and provenance) -> semver exact -> semver range -> profile_selector -> latest-compatible-fallback. This order balances reproducibility (digest) and usability (tags/semver).
We will adopt caret (^) compatibility for semver ranges by default for model packages, with a project-level override 'compat_policy' to allow tilde (~) or exact-only modes.

Performance profiles are first-class selectors. When a 'profile_selector' is provided, resolver will filter candidate artifacts by profile labels (e.g., 'latency:<50ms', 'cost:<0.5c/token', 'fp16-quantized') before applying precedence rules.

Ambiguous short commit hashes will result in 300ms heuristic expansion attempt on the catalog index, then a soft failure with suggestions; to resolve deterministically clients must use full hashes or digests.
We will publish resolution traces to audit logs (immutable) and make a condensed, human-readable trace available in SDK debug output.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Catalog schema update to include 'performance_profile' section and 'provenance.signature' fields. Backend migration + index rebuild (ETA 2 weeks).

Phase 2: Runtime resolver library (golang) implementing precedence order, semantic-range evaluator, profile filter, and signed provenance verifier. Unit tests and fuzzing for ambiguous inputs (ETA 3 weeks).

Phase 3: SDK surfaces new Pin type and helper: pinByTag(), pinBySemver(range), pinByHash(), pinByProfile(selector); add 'require_signed' option. Publish TypeScript and Python SDK changes (ETA 2 weeks).
Phase 4: Integration tests with Dedicated runtime and Private deployment; exercise canary rollouts with pinned variants and measure rollback behavior (ETA 2 weeks).
Phase 5: Docs, migration guide for existing tags/semver policies, and release notes.
progress_updates: 2026-02-22: Kickoff meeting with Catalog, Runtime, and SDK owners. Agreed on caret default for semver. Action: Catalog schema draft assigned to Leah Kim.

2026-02-28: Catalog schema PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/catalog/pull/312 (Leah). Draft adds performance_profile.{latency_ms,cost_per_token,throughput_rps,quantization} and provenance.signature fields.

2026-03-03: Runtime resolver prototype completed (golang) that resolves exact digests, full commit hashes, and simple tags. Basic audit log written to kinesis stream. Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/198
2026-03-07: SDK TypeScript pinBySemver(range) surface reviewed by DX team; feedback: include 'compat_policy' override and helper to pretty-print resolved trace. Assigned to Marco for follow-up.

2026-03-10: Unit test suite expanded to cover semver ranges; failing case discovered where two tags with identical timestamp exist for ephemeral model pushes. Decided to require tag creation timestamps to be unique or to fallback to digest ordering.
notes: Trade-offs considered: making profile selectors first-class improves ergonomics for latency-sensitive apps but can reduce reproducibility; mitigated by always returning an immutable digest in the resolution response.
We chose caret semantics because model authors tend to follow minor/patch compatibility when releasing iterations; however we will provide a per-model 'compat_policy' setting for strict users.
Open question: whether to allow fallback from profile_selector to semver ranges automatically; current plan is to not fallback across selector types unless client sets 'allow_fallbacks=true'.
